data.summary: The plan builds foundational concepts early, prioritizes the weak units (4 and 5) in the first half, and integrates the scheduled live classes. Each week balances topic study, practice problems, and review within a 5‑hour limit. The final two weeks focus on mixed review and timed practice to consolidate knowledge before the exam.

tasks: Read the textbook sections for 1.1, 1.2, and 1.5.
Do 15 free‑response style kinematics problems covering displacement, velocity, and 2‑D vectors.
Create a one‑page summary sheet of vector addition rules and common motion equations.
Watch Live Class 10000 and take notes on 4.1 and 4.2.
Complete the class worksheet (provided by instructor).
Do 10 FRQ problems on impulse and momentum change.
Review 4.3 conservation of linear momentum with 5 textbook examples.
Read sections 2.1‑2.2 and 2.5.
Draw free‑body diagrams for 8 different scenarios.
Solve 12 FRQs applying Newton's second law and system analysis.
Summarize the steps for solving dynamics problems on a one‑page cheat sheet.
Read textbook chapters for 3.1‑3.2 and 3.4.
Complete 10 energy‑conservation problems (incl. work‑energy theorem).
Calculate power for 5 real‑world situations.
Create a concept map linking kinetic energy, work, and conservation.

weeks.focus: Torque & Rotational Dynamics (weak unit) + Live class
tasks: Attend Live Class 10001; focus on 5.1 and 5.3 notes.
Do the class’s practice problems on rotational kinematics and torque.
Complete 8 FRQs on torque calculations and rotational inertia (5.4).
Build a quick reference table for torque = r×F and moment of inertia formulas.
Read sections 6.1, 6.3, 6.4.
Solve 10 problems on rotational kinetic energy and angular momentum conservation.
Watch a short video on angular impulse and complete the accompanying quiz.
Add rotational energy formulas to the cheat sheet created in week 1.
Read textbook for 7.1‑7.3.
Graph 6 simple harmonic motion examples (position, velocity, acceleration).
Do 12 FRQs on period, frequency, and energy of SHM.
Create flashcards for SHM equations and key terms.
Read sections 8.1‑8.2 and 8.4.
Complete 10 problems on pressure, buoyancy, and continuity equation.
Perform a quick lab‑style calculation: flow rate through a pipe using given diameters.
Summarize fluid‑law relationships on a one‑page sheet.
Take a 40‑minute mixed‑topic practice test (use past FRQs).
Mark answers against the scoring guide and note any recurring errors.
Review incorrect problems, re‑working each until correct.
Refresh cheat sheets and flashcards for all units.
Complete a full 90‑minute timed AP exam section covering the listed topics.
Score the section, calculate percent correct, and identify weak spots.
Do targeted drills (5 problems each) on any low‑scoring areas.
Write a one‑page summary of key strategies for the exam day.

data.final_week_advice: In the last week, simulate real exam conditions with timed sections, focus on accuracy, and use your cheat sheets only for quick checks. Get plenty of rest, review your error log, and enter the exam confident in your systematic problem‑solving process.
